dedupe_keys.name: a simulation of food supply chain netlogo model of supply chain structure and food quality safety in china

description: This NetLogo model simulates how the structure of a food supply chain evolves and what that means for food quality and safety in China. It was published in the CoMSES library in 2017 by Hang Xiong and Puqing Wang, with a companion paper in Chinese in the journal Agricultural Technology Economics (2015). There are three types of agents: producers, middlemen and government, standing for farmers, wholesalers and the food safety regulator. Two ways of managing the chain are compared, spot market transactions and contract transactions. Version 1.0.0 is available as a free download from CoMSES under the AFL-3.0 licence and needs NetLogo 5.0.5 or later. Caveats: the chain is stylised, and the paper is in Chinese. Coverage is China, in general terms. Simulation uses: comparing how contract and spot market chains perform, as a component of food supply resilience studies. Related records: the food supply chain resilience model (model-comses-food-supply-chain-resilience-efficiency) measures resilience of similar producer and trader networks.
inputs: Farmers, wholesalers and a food safety regulator
Spot market or contract transaction mode
